entry.title: Retrieval Without Regret: Calibrated Abstention for Long-Context Question Answering
entry.summary: Long-context language models answer many questions from the prompt alone, yet they retrieve anyway, paying latency for evidence they do not use. We study when retrieval helps and propose a calibrated abstention rule that predicts, from the model's own token-level uncertainty, whether the retrieved passages will change the answer. On three long-context benchmarks the rule skips 41% of retrievals with no loss in exact match, and its errors concentrate on questions the model answers wrongly with or without evidence.

entry.title: Tokenizer Drift: Measuring Vocabulary Mismatch Across Model Generations
entry.summary: Successive model generations ship new tokenizers, and downstream corpora tokenised for one generation are reused for the next. We define tokenizer drift as the divergence between the token distributions two tokenizers induce on the same text and show it predicts fine-tuning loss on transferred datasets better than vocabulary overlap does.

entry.title: Small Evaluators, Large Judgments: When a 1B Model Grades a 70B Model
entry.summary: We ask whether small models can serve as reliable judges of larger models' outputs. Across 12 tasks, a 1B judge agrees with human raters at 0.71 kappa on factual questions but drops to 0.38 on open-ended writing, and the gap is explained almost entirely by the judge's own ability to produce the reference.
